name: Anduril

summary.text: Anduril Industries is a privately held defense technology company founded in 2017 by Palmer Luckey and partners including Trae Stephens, a partner at Founders Fund, which has backed the company since its start. Its products include the Lattice software platform and autonomous sensor towers deployed for U.S. Customs and Border Protection. In 2025 it raised $2.5 billion at a $30.5 billion valuation, took over Microsoft's IVAS mixed-reality program for the U.S. Army, and won a $159 million Army prototype award under the Soldier Borne Mission Command program.

facts.claim: Founders Fund has backed Anduril since the company's start in 2017. Anduril co-founder Trae Stephens is a partner at Founders Fund.
facts.quote: Founders Fund has been a backer of Anduril since its start in 2017, and one of Anduril's co-founders, Trae Stephens, is a partner at the firm.

sources.title: Founders Fund in talks to back defense firm Anduril at $28 billion valuation, sources say

facts.claim: In June 2025 Anduril raised $2.5 billion in a Series G round at a $30.5 billion valuation, more than doubling its $14 billion valuation from its $1.5 billion raise the year before. The round included a $1 billion investment from Founders Fund, the largest single check the company had received.
facts.quote: Anduril secured the $30.5 billion valuation in its latest round, where it raised $2.5 billion... The round included a $1 billion investment from Founders Fund, the largest individual check the company has received to date.

sources.title: Anduril secures $30.5 billion valuation in latest fund raise
Defense tech unicorn Anduril doubles valuation

facts.claim: In February 2025 Microsoft announced a plan to transfer its U.S. Army IVAS (Integrated Visual Augmentation System) production contract, a 10-year deal valued at up to $22 billion, to Anduril. Breaking Defense reported in April 2025 that Anduril had assumed oversight of the production deal.
facts.quote: In February 2025, Microsoft said it wanted to move its IVAS production contract to Anduril... The original deal was a 10-year production contract valued up to $22 billion.

sources.title: Microsoft announces plan to slide $22 billion IVAS contract over to Anduril
Anduril gets green light from Army to take over Microsoft's IVAS project: Exec

facts.claim: In May 2025 Anduril and Meta teamed up to pursue the Army's Soldier Borne Mission Command (SBMC) competition, the successor to IVAS, and submitted a white paper to the service. Anduril is expected to develop the program's network portion in part with its Lattice software platform.
facts.quote: Anduril is expected to develop the network portion of the program, in part, with its Lattice software platform. Anduril and Meta also teamed up to pursue the SBMC competition, and they have already submitted a white paper to the service.

sources.title: Anduril, Meta team up for Army IVAS recompete

facts.claim: In September 2025 the Army awarded more than $350 million in prototype contracts under the Soldier Borne Mission Command program; Anduril announced a $159 million deal and Rivet a $195 million agreement.
facts.quote: The Army has awarded a total of more than $350 million in contracts to industry teams for the SBMC program. Anduril announced a $159 million deal, and Rivet announced a $195 million agreement.

sources.title: Army awards more than $350M in contracts for Soldier Borne Mission Command system prototypes

facts.claim: U.S. Customs and Border Protection awarded Anduril a $363 million contract for more than 200 Extended Range Sentry Towers, 80-foot towers that integrate with existing Sentry tower networks and Anduril's Lattice software. The relationship began in 2019 with five test towers, became a program of record in 2020, and Anduril said in late 2024 it had deployed its 300th tower to CBP.
facts.quote: The XRST integrates with existing Sentry tower networks and Anduril's Lattice software to enhance counter-intrusion capabilities... The award expands a relationship that began in 2019 with five test towers.

sources.title: CBP awards Anduril $363M contract for Extended Range Sentry Towers

facts.claim: CBP awarded Anduril $25 million in July 2020 and a further $36 million in September 2020 for its sensor towers. Data from the towers feeds into Lattice, which alerts operators; in a border scenario the system sends location data to Border Patrol agents' phones when it believes it has detected a person crossing.
facts.quote: In a border scenario, the system sends location data to Border Patrol agents' phones when it believes it has detected a human crossing.

openQuestions: The $363 million Extended Range Sentry Tower award is reported without a clear date; confirm the award date and value on CBP or USAspending records.

The page links Anduril to Peter Thiel personally; sources here only establish Founders Fund (Thiel's firm) as an investor and Trae Stephens as a Founders Fund partner. A direct Thiel–Anduril relationship needs its own source.
No source was found tying Anduril to the Pentagon's Replicator initiative specifically; the page's claim that Replicator contracts went to Anduril, Palantir and Shield AI is unsourced here.
